rows.text: Are there any foods or tablets that don't agree with you?
Did the last course of tablets give you any trouble, like itching or a swollen mouth?
Is there a medicine you have to avoid?
Do you carry an adrenaline pen for anything?
Has anything ever made you feel your chest closing up?
So the dye they gave you for the scan made you sick and itchy, I'll flag it.
Tell me about any bad experiences with medicines.
Do you react to the sticky tape on dressings?
Could you spell your surname for me and say when you were born?
I've got two Patels on the list, which one are you?
Let's make sure the label on your wrist is yours.
Can you read me the details on the strap round your wrist?
What's your full name, as it would be on your passport?
Just confirming who you are before I go on: name and birth date.
Does the name on this tag belong to you?
Can you tell me your address and the date of your birth for the check?
Are you comfortable with us starting?
Is there anything stopping you from agreeing to the operation?
If you are happy, scribble your name on the dotted line.
So, are we doing this?
I'll need you to say you accept the risks before we continue.
Do you want us to carry on or would you rather stop?
You're content for the team to go ahead, aren't you?
Give me a nod and we'll begin the anaesthetic.
He has had a bowl of porridge at seven.
She says she finished a packet of mints on the ward.
Heads up, he snuck a pasty from the canteen at eleven.
She drank a glass of milk at breakfast time.
His stomach isn't empty, he ate dinner late last night and breakfast too.
He's been grazing on grapes all morning.
They gave her a snack on the ward at ten.
He's eaten lunch, I saw him.
She's quickly getting sicker.
His lips have gone blue.
Her heart rate has doubled in the last hour.
He's gasping for air now.
She's drifting off and won't wake properly.
Her temperature has shot up and she's shaking.
His oxygen reading keeps falling whatever I do.
She's breathing very slowly and looks pale.
Let me paint the picture for you: elderly woman, abdominal pain, day two.
Where we are is a planned case that has been delayed twice.
The thing I'd ask is that someone senior reviews her before theatre.
From a background point of view, he is otherwise fit and well.
My overall impression is of a stable patient.
What I'm hoping for is a review before lunch.
To set the scene, he came in last night with right-sided pain.
Going forward I suggest we repeat the bloods.
